_doc: fc-parallel-006 (filesystem): list + 2x delete; depends_on_order: true. The prompt names the specific files to delete but instructs the model to list first; the expected calls are list_directory then 2x delete_file in that exact order. Order matters because the prompt's 'first... then' phrasing makes the list step a verification, not a discoverable step (the files are named). Tests that the model can do 3 calls in the right order, not just 1 or 2. ORDER CONTRACT (M1, PR #31): the scorer (#19) only has two modes — order-insensitive (depends_on_order absent/false) and strict positional (true). This case needs 'list before deletes', which order-insensitive cannot express (it would wrongly pass delete-before-list), so we keep strict positional. To avoid over-constraining the two same-phase deletes, the prompt pins their literal order ('...1.0... then ...1.1...'); the model is expected to follow the prompt's listing order. A future depends_on_order: 'partial' knob in #19 would let the two deletes be mutually unordered.
prompt: First list the contents of /tmp/old-builds/ to see what's there. Then delete /tmp/old-builds/app-1.0.tar.gz, then /tmp/old-builds/app-1.1.tar.gz, in that order.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the full text contents of a file at the given absolute path. Returns the file contents as a UTF-8 string, or an error if the file does not exist or is not readable.

function.name: list_directory
function.description: List the names of entries (files and subdirectories) directly inside the given absolute directory path. Non-recursive.

function.name: delete_file
function.description: Delete a file at the given absolute path. Irreversible. Returns an error if the file does not exist, if the path is a directory, or if the caller lacks write permission.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to delete
